problem.text: Module saving prefixed the filename with work_dir twice: main() constructed a work-relative destination, then save_tensor() joined work_dir again. Ordinary relative working directories therefore targeted an unintended nested directory.

reasoning.text: The fix leaves path resolution in save_tensor() and passes only qtensors/<module-key>.safetensors from main(), matching the helper's existing checkpoint caller rather than changing the shared helper.

impact.text: The corrected destination matches the qtensors directory created by prepare_env(). Tensor collection and serialization are unchanged.

source_notes.text: The earlier conversion entry identified this relative-path hazard; the task removes that specific hazard.

limitations: Validation models POSIX path joining only; no safetensors write, model conversion, GPU execution or interruption/recovery test was run.

claims.text: main() merges each module's get_tensors() results into a dictionary and passes it to save_tensor(), whose dictionary branch writes the named tensors with save_file(). The patch changes only the filename argument, so the correction applies to every processed module reaching this save point, not just modules with quantization targets.

A standard-library transcription produced work/work/qtensors/layer.safetensors before the patch and work/qtensors/layer.safetensors afterward. For /tmp/work both expressions produced the same absolute destination; for '.' they normalized identically. Thus the commit message's 'double absolute path' wording describes redundant construction, but the demonstrated destination error concerns relative paths.

The inspected CLI entrypoint calls prepare() and then main(). The other direct save_tensor() caller already supplies ckpt_new/state.safetensors relative to work_dir and is unchanged. The patch does not alter checkpoint rotation or resume loading.

findings.description: The inherited interruption window in checkpoint rotation remains unchanged by this path fix.
findings.trigger: Conversion is interrupted after renaming ckpt to ckpt_old but before renaming ckpt_new to ckpt, then the user resumes.
findings.expected_behavior: Resume recovers an available complete checkpoint.
findings.actual_behavior: prepare() loads ckpt/job.json without falling back to ckpt_old or ckpt_new; prepare_env() can recreate an empty ckpt directory, but not its missing job.json.

verification.description: Inspected the two sequential renames, resume loader and CLI calls; the complete task diff changes only the module-save filename. Reach is the inspected conversion CLI's checkpoint/resume workflow.
verification.limits: No interruption was injected; literal caller search does not establish all external callers.

annotation.summary: Fixes duplicated working-directory prefixes when saving converted module tensors, preserving absolute-path destinations and the shared serialization helper.

argv:
import posixpath as p
for w in ['work','/tmp/work','.']:
 old=p.join(w,p.join(w,'qtensors','layer.safetensors'))
 new=p.join(w,'qtensors/layer.safetensors')
 print(repr(w), 'old='+old, 'new='+new, 'equivalent='+str(p.normpath(old)==p.normpath(new)))
